entries.test: Alexa's feature-release history before November 2022 and contemporary comparisons of Alexa's conversational capabilities with GPT-3 would test the claim.
entries.note: The comparison concerns conversational capability in context.

entries.test: Public technical accounts of Alexa's architecture and development constraints could establish whether scaling was the principal obstacle to conversational capability in November 2022.
entries.note: The normalization removes 'I don't think' and broadens an Amazon-focused explanation to smart assistants generally.

entries.test: Contemporary LLM reliability evaluations and public studies of assistant retention under frequent errors would test the reliability and user-abandonment assertions.
entries.note: The record combines an observation with a causal conditional and generalizes Alexa to assistants like Alexa.

entries.test: Publicly documented LLM safeguards available in November 2022 and demonstrated failures would test whether any known method guaranteed avoidance of all three behaviors.
entries.note: The source specifies 100% avoidance; 'reliably' weakens that absolute threshold.

entries.test: Galactica's publicly recorded outputs and launch history would establish whether it substantially failed to prevent harmful advice and fabricated information.
entries.note: 'In this regard' refers to the preceding three behaviors, including insulting users; the normalization narrows that reference. 'Epic' intensifies an otherwise factual product-performance claim.
The harms are possibilities. The added deterrence conclusion loses the framing as one of his 'best guesses.'

entries.test: Public user studies following a freely conversational Alexa release could measure whether expectations rose substantially and whether most expected tasks exceeded its capabilities.
entries.note: The antecedent describes a possible deployment, rather than merely assigning a probability to the outcome.

entries.test: Public demonstrations and reliability evaluations of November 2022 LLM action-control systems would establish whether sentence outputs required a separate interpreter and whether reliable interpretation was known.
entries.note: The source specifically discusses sentence outputs and explicitly allows a separate parsing system; the normalization broadens this to all LLM outputs.

entries.test: Contemporary evaluations of GPT-3-class models on user-intent recognition and instruction interpretation would test their reliability for that function.
entries.note: In context, 'great tech' concerns functional reliability rather than aesthetic worth. The present-tense assertion is separable from the speculative parenthetical.
'May never' states a possibility, not a firm prediction.

entries.test: The release date and public reliability and deployment evidence for an LLM conversational home-control product capable of serving millions of homes would establish how far away that capability was from November 2022.
entries.note: This is a firm forecast with an imprecise horizon, not an explicit deadline.

entries.test: Public comparative safety evaluations of LLM-controlled robots and conversational home assistants would test whether robotic embodiment increases the likelihood or severity of harmful failures.
entries.note: The comparative risk assertion uses 'would'; 'might' describes the preceding reference to possible events.
